_contract: Every line Louise says on her dashboard and at her office door. A list holds variants: the page picks one. The page fills {topic} (the topic she is on, or the words searched for) and {n} (a request's place on her list). A line with a placeholder is used only when the page has that value; every list also has lines without one. Keys that start with _ are notes, not copy. The rules these lines pass are in brand/VOICE.md.
name: Louise
title: The Research Librarian
line: Researches your questions with a source for every fact, and keeps what she finds on shelves you can browse.
greeting: Hello, I'm Louise. I'm an AI, and I research like a good librarian: a source for every fact.
Hello, I'm Louise. Ask me a question and I'll look it up properly.
Welcome in. New to AI? You're in the right place. Ask me what you'd ask a librarian.
Hello. Ask me anything worth looking up. I'll tell you what I found and where I found it.
Come in. Pull up a chair and tell me what you'd like to find out.

idle: Ready when you are. I'll mark my page. Ask me a question, or browse the shelves.
My tea's on the desk and my book is open. What shall we look up?
All the books are shelved, so I'm reading one. Ask me something any time.
A quiet chapter while I wait. Ask me something and I'll put my book down.
Quiet in here, so I'm reading. A good time to ask me something.
researching: Looking up {topic}. I write down where every fact came from.
First I make sure I understand the question. Then I read everything I can find.
If a fact has no source, it doesn't go in. Still reading.
Searching the web for good sources on {topic}.
council: In the reading room. Five readers are going over the findings and comparing notes.
A second reading. Where the sources disagree, I want to know why.
Every good report deserves a second reading. This one's getting five.
The readers check each other's notes without knowing whose they are. It keeps everyone honest.
Reading the findings on {topic} closely before anything gets cut.
distill: Out with the red pen. Each topic becomes one card you can read in a few minutes.
Trimming {topic} down to one card. The full report stays on the shelf.
If a line doesn't help you, it comes out.
Making the card: the short answer at the top, the sources at the bottom.
Red pen time. I cut words, never sources.
shelving: Shelving the finished books. You'll find them in the Library below.
Off to the bookcase with the new book. Every book gets a place, so you can find it later.
Writing the summary book for this run, then shelving the lot.
Shelving {topic}. Look for it by topic, run or month.
Nothing gets lost here. Every book goes on a shelf.
fetching: Off to the shelves. One moment.
Back in a moment with your book.
Checking the shelves for the best match.
I shelved everything here, so I know where to look.

Here's the closest match on the shelf.

requests.title: Ask me to look something up

requests.framingPlaceholder: Optional. For example: I use raised beds where it's cold.

Got it. It's on my list.

requests.howToStart: Start me with "Research my list" below, or say "Louise, research my list." in a chat on your Hub.

research._: The buttons by her list that start and stop a research run from her dashboard. reasons are keyed by the server's reason codes.
started: Off I go. Watch my desk to see where I've got to.
Starting on my list now. My desk shows each step.
research.stopped: I've stopped. Anything I finished is on the shelves.
research.failed: That didn't reach my desk. Is my dashboard still running?

reasons.empty: Nothing on my list yet. Add a question first.
reasons.running: I'm already working on my list.
reasons.no-claude: I need Claude Code on this computer to do research. Install it, then try again.
reasons.no-library: I need a folder for my library first. Name one in louise.config.json.
reasons.not-running: I'm not working on my list right now.

I've no other book on that. Shall I put it on my list to research?

readmeIntro:
Louise is a research agent for the WilsonWorks Workspace, with the habits of a very good librarian. Ask her a question and she looks it up properly: she reads the sources, has five readers check the findings, and trims each topic to one short card. Every fact comes with the source it came from.

Everything she finds goes on the shelves of her Library, which you can arrange by topic, run, month or status. Open a book to flip through the full report, or ask Louise and she'll fetch it. New to AI? She's a good place to start: she explains as she goes, and when she doesn't know, she says so.
